title: Manager Activation & Feedback Architecture
author: Priya Menon
content:
Purpose

This document defines the Manager Activation & Feedback Architecture: a repeatable, measurable approach to launching managers into new roles and establishing a feedback system that scales across distributed teams. It treats the manager ramp as an "architecture" with clearly defined phases, "performance gateways" (decision points), tooling integrations, and asynchronous templates for high-signal feedback.

Scope

- Applies to all people-managers at Redwood Inference (new hires, internal moves, and promoted contributors moving into management).
- Designed for distributed teams and hybrid work patterns; supports asynchronous feedback where required.
- Complements (but does not replace) 1:1 coaching from People Partners and any role-specific technical onboarding.

Principles

1. Outcome-first: Ramp success is measured by outcomes (team onboarding velocity, stakeholder satisfaction, key hires closed), not just completion of tasks.
2. Observable signals: Define 5–7 measurable signals per manager that gate progress at each phase.
3. Lightweight governance: Decision gateways must be quick (≤ 2 days) and data-driven.
4. Distributed feedback: Enable peers and reports to contribute structured input asynchronously.
5. Role-specific flexibility: Standard architecture with configurable cells for different functions (Eng, Product, CS).

Manager Activation Phases (Architecture View)

1) Pre-Start (T-minus 2 weeks)
- People Ops: create role onboarding pack, invite to role-specific Slack channel, provision access to org charts, OKR history, and hiring pipeline.
- Manager: review direct reports' current OKRs, backlog of high-priority tickets, and current 1-on-1 cadence notes.
- Owners: People Ops (create pack), Hiring Manager (intro doc), IT (access).

2) Launch Week (Day 0–7) — Orientation + Rapid Listening
Goals: introduce org context, establish 1:1s, document initial hypotheses about team health.
Key activities:
- 1:1 with each direct report (30–45m) — discover top 3 blockers and perceived priorities.
- Stakeholder syncs (Product/Eng counterpart leads) — align on dependencies.
- Team readout: manager shares a 30/60/90 draft with team for feedback.

3) Establishment (Week 2–8) — Baseline & Initial Actions
Goals: implement first set of small experiments (communication norms, meeting cadence), close early hires if assigned.
Signals (examples):
- 1:1 completion rate >= 80% for first 4 weeks
- Team survey NPS >= -10 (or improvement of >= 10 points vs baseline)
- Hiring pipeline moves (first offer extended or candidate shortlists updated)

4) Performance Gateway "Gate A" (End of Week 8) — Go/Iterate
Gate A decision factors (collect data 1 week prior):
- Evidence packet (see "Gate Evidence Template")
- People Ops review + skip-level input
- Hiring velocity and onboarding of new joiners
Decisions: continue with plan, trigger targeted coaching plan (30 days), or escalate to People Partner for re-evaluation.

5) Optimization (Month 3–6) — Scale & Stabilize
- Focus on team-level metrics: cycle time, MTTI for incidents, delivery predictability.
- Introduce manager-level OKRs aligned to org priorities.
- Gate B (end of month 6): verify sustained signals and readiness for full autonomy.

Performance Gate: Evidence Template (what to gather)

- Short executive summary (1 paragraph)
- 1:1 schedule + notes anonymized (redacted where necessary)
- Team survey results and commentary (or documented skip-level feedback)
- Hiring pipeline snapshot (candidates, stages, offers)
- 2–3 examples of decisions with outcomes (e.g., reprioritized roadmap item, resolved incident)
- People Ops assessment checklist (completed vs outstanding items)

Operational Runbook: Manager Handoff Protocol

1. Submit Handoff Packet (by outgoing manager or hiring manager)
   - Who: Outgoing manager / Hiring manager; Owner (People Ops) verifies completeness.
   - Packet includes: role charter, org chart, active projects, open performance flags, hiring notes, and access/credentials inventory.

2. Handoff Meeting (60m)
   - Participants: Incoming manager, outgoing manager (if available), People Partner, HRIS admin, relevant TLs.
   - Agenda: critical risks, immediate actions (first week), personnel sensitivities, pending escalations.

3. Slack & Systems Transfer
   - IT ensures role-based groups added, calendar delegations set, and repo permissions validated.

4. Sign-off and Kickoff
   - People Ops marks the role as "Active" in the Manager Ramp tracker and schedules Gate A review date.

Asynchronous Feedback Architecture

- Use structured templates for all asynchronous inputs. Templates are short, answerable in 3–5 bullets, and designed for low friction. Example: "Rapid Signal Template" (used for skip-level or peer feedback)
  1) One sentence summary of relationship/context.
  2) One achievement in last 30 days.
  3) One observable improvement opportunity (concrete behavior).
  4) One suggested action for manager.

- Collection channels:
  - Anonymous survey (People Ops-owned) at Gate A and Gate B
  - Slack pulse channel (#manager-feedback-{team}) for lightweight, non-anonymous signals
  - Synced notes in the Manager Ramp tracker (consolidated by People Ops)

Templates and Commands

- Sample 30/60/90 JSON snippet (for automation):
{
  "name": "30-60-90-snapshot",
  "owner": "Manager",
  "30_days": ["Listening tour","stabilize 1:1s"],
  "60_days": ["deliver small win","address key hiring gaps"],
  "90_days": ["measure impact","set manager OKRs"]
}

- People Ops CLI exports (example):
$ peopleops export-manager-ramp --manager="Evan Carter" --format=csv --since=2028-01-01

Escalations and Exceptions

- If a Gate decision requires escalation: People Ops + direct VP triage within 3 business days.
- Exceptions (e.g., high-risk roles, interim managers, major restructuring) get a shortened Gate cadence: Gate A at 4 weeks, Gate B at 12 weeks.

Measurement and Success Metrics

Primary measures (tracked in People Ops dashboard):
- Manager ramp completion rate (Gate A pass within 8 weeks) — Target: 85%
- Direct report retention at 6 months — Target: >= 95%
- Cross-team stakeholder satisfaction (quarterly poll) — Target: >= 4.0/5
- Hiring velocity (time-to-offer for open slots owned by manager) — Target: median <= 45 days

Implementation Plan & Timeline

- Q3 2028: Pilot with Eng & Product managers (10 managers) — collect Gate A/B signals and refine templates.
- Q4 2028: Full rollout to all new people-managers; automate tracker integrations (HRIS + Slack).
- Q1 2029: Add team-level OKR ingestion to evidence pack and run first cross-org calibration.

Ownership & Review

- Document owner: People Ops (Priya Menon).
- Gate decision authority: People Partner + Hiring Manager (VP-level escalation as required).
- Review cadence: annual review of templates and signals or after each pilot cohort.

Appendix: Quick Reference Cards

- "Gate A quick checklist" (one-pager sent as PDF): 6 items — 1:1 completion, skip-level pulse, survey, hiring snapshot, two sample decisions, People Ops assessment.
- "Asynchronous Feedback guide": 3 templates (Rapid Signal, Manager Check, Candidate Flag).
